_comment: SQL translator literal-safe rewrite + BIGINT autoincrement contract --
feature 7. Three owner-decided items (OWNER-DECISIONS.md Batch 5; feature doc
007-sql-translator.md SQLTRANS-DEC-01/02/03), proven against REAL databases
(NO mocks) -- every case RUNS a translated statement on the real engine and
checks the rows/DDL, never a string comparison alone.
SQLTRANS-DEC-01 -- the DATA-CORRUPTION fix. The dialect rewrites (|| -> CONCAT,
ILIKE -> LOWER LIKE, TRUE/FALSE -> 1/0) used to MANGLE STRING LITERALS: a
column value of 'a||b', a label 'TRUE', or a LIKE pattern that mentions
ILIKE was rewritten as if it were SQL, because none of the transforms masked
string literals/comments before matching. concat additionally split the
WHOLE statement on || so `SELECT a || b FROM t` became
`CONCAT(SELECT a, b FROM t)` (invalid SQL). All four now mask literals/
comments -> rewrite -> restore, and concat rewrites only the operand chain
(Python `_mask_literals`, PHP `maskLiterals`, Ruby `mask_literals`, Node
`maskLiterals`). The multi-word ILIKE pattern that the old greedy \S+
truncated now survives whole.
SQLTRANS-DEC-02 -- the Ruby unwiring + dead/duplicated code. concat/bool/ilike
are WIRED into the MySQL query path in Ruby (MysqlDriver#translate_dialect on
execute_query/execute) and PHP (MySQLAdapter::translateDialect on query/
execute), matching the already-wired Python/Node adapters, so a portable ||
or ILIKE query RUNS on real MySQL in all four (before: MySQL read a bare ||
as logical OR and rejected ILIKE). Ruby's dead+wrong translator methods were
DELETED -- limit_to_rows, limit_to_top, placeholder_style (the Ruby drivers
own pagination via SELECT FIRST/SKIP + OFFSET/FETCH and placeholders via
?/$1, and these helpers emitted a different, inferior shape that nothing
called) -- plus the duplicate SQLTranslator.query_key (QueryCache.query_key
is the one live cache key). Less code, one source per concern.
SQLTRANS-DEC-03 -- BIGINT autoincrement. `BIGINT PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` now
yields a real 64-bit auto-increment column per dialect: PostgreSQL BIGSERIAL
(was a plain BIGINT with the keyword stripped -- no sequence, so an insert
with no id failed the NOT NULL key), MySQL BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT (preserved
via the generic replace; locked here for parity). The UPSERT/ON CONFLICT and
date/time-function omissions stay documented in 007-sql-translator.md.
MAINTAINABILITY (owner directive): ONE translator path per backend, ZERO new
runtime dependencies -- the literal-safe rewrite reuses each language's own
regex/string handling; the MySQL wiring is a no-op unless a ||/ILIKE token is
present, so ordinary queries are untouched.
NO MOCKS. The lab runs the suites against real PostgreSQL :55432 (tina4/tina4)
and MySQL :3306 (tina4/tina4 -> tina4_test). The concat/ilike cases go THROUGH
the real MySQL adapter (db.fetch), the boolean case translates then executes
on real MySQL, and the BIGINT case executes the translated DDL then inserts
with no id and reads back a generated 64-bit id + introspects the column type
on real PostgreSQL and MySQL. MSSQL/Firebird are deliberately out of this gate
(the fix is engine-agnostic; MySQL+PostgreSQL exercise every code path).
Mutation-proved (all four): revert the literal-safe rewrite to the old naive
one and 'pipes inside a string literal are preserved' goes RED (the || inside
'a||b' is wrongly turned into CONCAT and the query errors / returns nothing),
'concat pipes translate outside literals and run' goes RED (the whole
statement is wrapped in CONCAT -> invalid SQL), 'boolean token inside a string
literal is preserved' goes RED ('TRUE' becomes '1' and the row is not found),
and 'ilike pattern with multiple words survives and runs' goes RED (the greedy
\S+ truncates '%two words%'). Revert the PostgreSQL BIGINT branch and 'bigint
autoincrement creates a real bigint column' goes RED (the insert with no id
violates the NOT NULL key).
Each invariant names a REAL suite file per framework carrying the SAME case
names in each language's own idiom, which scripts/audit-contract-fixtures.py
normalises and matches.
feature: 7 - SQL translator (literal-safe concat/bool/ilike rewrite + Ruby wiring/dead-code removal + BIGINT autoincrement)

invariants.rule: The dialect rewrites are LITERAL-SAFE: || -> CONCAT, TRUE/FALSE -> 1/0 and ILIKE -> LOWER() LIKE LOWER() NEVER touch text inside a string literal, quoted identifier or comment, and concat rewrites only the || operand chain -- never the whole statement. A multi-word ILIKE pattern is captured whole. concat/ilike are WIRED into the MySQL query path in all four (Python `_translate_sql`, Node `translateSql`, PHP `MySQLAdapter::translateDialect`, Ruby `MysqlDriver#translate_dialect`), so a portable `||`/`ILIKE` query RUNS on real MySQL. Identical rewrite in all four (Python/Node/PHP/Ruby SQLTranslator.concat_pipes_to_func / booleanToInt / ilike_to_like via a mask-literals helper).
invariants.why: A rewrite that edits text INSIDE a string literal is silent data corruption -- a stored value 'a||b', a label 'TRUE', or a LIKE pattern mentioning ILIKE is DATA, and the query then returns the wrong rows or fails outright; the whole-statement concat split emitted invalid SQL on EVERY MySQL/MSSQL statement containing `||`. Proven against a REAL MySQL, no mocks: the row keyed on 'a||b' is found (the literal survived), a `first || ' ' || last` chain returns the joined value (concat ran and did not wrap the statement), a multi-word ILIKE returns its row, and a bare TRUE became 1 while the literal 'TRUE' was preserved. Mutation-proved: revert to the naive rewrite and these cases go RED.
cases: concat pipes translate outside literals and run
pipes inside a string literal are preserved
ilike pattern with multiple words survives and runs
boolean token inside a string literal is preserved

invariants.rule: A `BIGINT PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` DDL translates to a real 64-bit auto-increment column per dialect: PostgreSQL BIGSERIAL, MySQL BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT stays SERIAL / INT AUTO_INCREMENT). Identical in all four (SQLTranslator.auto_increment_syntax / autoIncrementSyntax postgresql branch handles BIGINT -> BIGSERIAL in addition to INTEGER -> SERIAL).
invariants.why: Before the fix, PostgreSQL only special-cased INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT; a BIGINT just had the keyword stripped, leaving a plain BIGINT primary key with NO sequence -- so an insert with no id violates the NOT NULL key and a 64-bit auto-increment column is silently unusable. Proven against a REAL PostgreSQL and MySQL, no mocks: the translated DDL executes, an insert with NO id auto-generates one, and information_schema reports the column type as bigint. Mutation-proved: revert the PostgreSQL BIGINT branch and this case goes RED (the insert fails the NOT NULL key).
cases: bigint autoincrement creates a real bigint column
